title: De la démonomanie des sorciers
author: Jean Bodin
epithet: The jurist's case for burning the witch
summary: Bodin's demonology, written by one of the age's foremost political theorists as a direct answer to the sceptics — a learned and pitiless argument that witchcraft is real and its punishment a duty, and a chief authority cited in the persecutions.

title: Tableau de l'inconstance des mauvais anges et démons
author: Pierre de Lancre
query: Tableau de l'inconstance des mauvais anges Lancre
epithet: The Basque witch-hunt set down by its inquisitor
summary: De Lancre's account of the mass witch trials he conducted in the Pays de Labourd — a lurid, systematic description of the sabbath, famous for the fold-out engraving of the witches' assembly.

title: Nova de universis philosophia
author: Francesco Patrizi
epithet: A Neoplatonic cosmos of light against Aristotle
summary: Patrizi's system, which sought to replace Aristotle in the schools with a philosophy of light descending from God through the world — and which appended the Hermetic and Zoroastrian texts as older and truer than the Greeks.

title: Natural Magick
author: Giambattista della Porta
epithet: The English Magia Naturalis, twenty books of wonders
summary: The English 'Natural Magick', della Porta's twenty books of the secrets of nature — optics, magnetism, cookery, counterfeiting gold — the Renaissance encyclopaedia of natural marvels for the English reader.
imprint: London: for Thomas Young and Samuel Speed, 1658

title: Daemonologie
author: King James VI
epithet: A king's dialogue proving witchcraft real
summary: James VI of Scotland's dialogue on witchcraft, necromancy and the powers of spirits — written to refute the sceptics, and the royal authority behind the trials and the 1604 Witchcraft Act.

title: The Anatomy of Melancholy
author: Robert Burton
epithet: Melancholy, its demons, spirits and cures
summary: Burton's vast anatomy of melancholy, whose long digression on spirits, devils, magicians and astrology is one of the richest surveys of Renaissance occult belief ever assembled.

title: The Vanity of Arts and Sciences
author: Henry Cornelius Agrippa
query: Vanity of Arts and Sciences Agrippa
epithet: Agrippa's recantation of all human learning
summary: The English 'Vanity of Arts and Sciences', Agrippa's sceptical demolition of every branch of knowledge including his own magic — the recantation that shadowed the Occult Philosophy.

title: Of Ghostes and Spirites Walking by Nyght
author: Ludwig Lavater
query: Of Ghostes and Spirites Walking by Nyght Lavater
summary: Lavater's treatise on nocturnal apparitions and their causes — a Protestant attempt to explain hauntings without Catholic purgatory, and a source Shakespeare drew on for his ghosts.

title: A Treatise of Specters or Straunge Sights
author: Pierre Le Loyer
query: A Treatise of Specters Le Loyer
epithet: A learned inquiry into visions and phantoms
summary: Le Loyer's learned survey of specters, visions and apparitions across history and philosophy — a compendium of Renaissance thought on the boundary of the seen and unseen, in English.

title: The Terrors of the Night
author: Thomas Nashe
query: The Terrors of the Night Nashe
epithet: A wit's discourse on dreams and apparitions
summary: Nashe's brilliant discourse on dreams, nightmares and the spirits that trouble sleep — a sceptical, dazzling Elizabethan essay on the psychology of the night's terrors.

title: Pseudodoxia Epidemica
author: Thomas Browne
epithet: The great catalogue of vulgar errors
summary: Browne's examination of the 'vulgar errors' of his age — amulets, the basilisk, sympathetic magic, astrology — weighing each against reason and experiment; a monument of early scientific scepticism.

title: A Dialogue concerning Witches and Witchcraftes
author: George Gifford
epithet: A country minister on the folly of witch-belief
summary: Gifford's dialogue on the popular belief in witches — sceptical of the accusations while granting the Devil's power — one of the shrewdest Elizabethan discussions of the witch panic.

title: A Discourse of the Damned Art of Witchcraft
author: William Perkins
query: Discourse of the Damned Art of Witchcraft Perkins
epithet: The Puritan casebook against the witch
summary: Perkins's systematic Puritan treatise on witchcraft — its covenant with Satan, its detection and its punishment — the theological handbook behind much English witch-prosecution.

title: The Castle of Knowledge
author: Robert Recorde
query: The Castle of Knowledge Recorde astronomy
epithet: The first English textbook of the heavens
summary: Recorde's dialogue teaching the sphere and the motions of the heavens — the first astronomy in English, and an early notice of Copernicus, from the man who invented the equals sign.

title: A Brief and Pleasant Treatise of Natural and Artificial Conclusions
author: Thomas Hill
query: Natural and Artificial Conclusions Thomas Hill
epithet: A popular book of natural marvels and tricks
summary: Hill's popular collection of natural 'conclusions' — experiments, tricks and marvels of household natural magic — the Elizabethan best-seller that put the secrets of nature in every hand.
